clue.text: Academic boss wanting acknowledgments of indebtedness

parts.note: a stud is a boss in the sense of a raised knob or ornament
IOUs are written notes acknowledging a debt, from 'I owe you'

explanation.surface: A university head who refuses to accept any thanks or debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests a head of department, but it is the metalwork sense: a knob or stud.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly, bookish person can be described as academic.

clue.text: Sidney holds set-up to be quite senseless

indicators.note: Sidney's short form holds another piece between its letters, so it is the container

parts.note: Sid is the usual short form of the name Sidney

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' tells us the word for set is written from the bottom upward

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: Someone named Sidney thinks an arrangement makes no sense at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set-up' reads as a scheme, but splits into 'set' and 'up', the reversal signal in a down clue; 'holds' makes Sidney's short form the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid means foolish, lacking all good sense.

clue.text: Push to produce an effect

indicators.note: to produce is to work up or bring forth, so the letters of the two words are made into something new

explanation.surface: A shove made in order to get some result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' rearranges the letters of PUSH TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An upshot is the eventual result or outcome of something.

clue.text: No degrees needed to be top like this!

definitions.text: No degrees needed to be top like this!

parts.words: No degrees needed to be top like this!
parts.note: zero degrees Celsius is freezing, and a covering on the top of a polar region is made at that temperature

explanation.surface: A remark that you need no qualifications to reach the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No degrees' suggests a lack of university qualifications, but means a temperature of nought, at which water freezes; 'top' is a cap, here at the poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent mass of frozen water covers the top of the globe at each pole.

clue.text: Sleep on it

parts.note: read literally, this is bedding you lie upon at night, rather than advice to delay a decision

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep on it' is usually advice to wait before deciding; here it describes the lower piece of bed linen.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom piece of bed linen is the one a sleeper lies on.

clue.text: Very large watch made on the Continent

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
to tend is to watch over or look after

explanation.surface: An oversized timepiece manufactured in mainland Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a timepiece but is a verb, to look after. OSTEND is a Belgian port, and 'the Continent' is the British name for mainland Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Belgian ferry port across the Channel from Britain lies in mainland Europe.

clue.text: True art back in view

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the word for view

parts.note: a sight is a view or something seen

indicators.note: back means the word art is written in reverse order

explanation.surface: Genuine art is once more on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns ART to TRA, which goes 'in' SIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight can mean honest or truthful, as in a straight answer.

clue.text: Involves outside right-and insides

indicators.note: the word for involves sits outside the letter for right, enclosing it

parts.note: to entail something is to involve it as a consequence

explanation.surface: Something that covers both the exterior and the interior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' puts ENTAILS round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the internal organs, the guts of an animal.

clue.text: Making loss, paid in settlement

indicators.note: making signals that the letters given are used to make up a new word

explanation.surface: A business losing money but paying out to resolve a claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' rearranges the letters of LOSS and PAID. 'Settlement' reads as a payout, but the definition is the settling of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposal is the arranging or settling of a matter, as in disposal of an estate.

clue.text: A French male stayed awfully insecure

parts.note: un is the French word for 'a' used before masculine nouns

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of the word are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who remained, feeling very uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges STAYED into STEADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsteady is wobbly, not firmly fixed in place.

clue.text: Talks at some length of money and taxes

parts.note: P stands for penny or pence, a unit of money
rates are local property taxes in Britain

explanation.surface: Lengthy discussions about finance and taxation.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were British local taxes on property.
explanation.definitionFit: To prate is to chatter on foolishly and at length.

clue.text: Adroitly affecting great love

indicators.note: affecting can mean altering, so the letters of the word are changed around

explanation.surface: Skilfully pretending to feel deep affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affecting' rearranges ADROITLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is excessive admiration or worship of a person or thing.

clue.text: Scold when six tease duck

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to rag someone is to tease them
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so O

explanation.surface: A nagging when six people make fun of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, bad-tempered woman, a scold or shrew.

clue.text: Travellers' accommodation accorded acclaim for a change

parts.note: an inn provides lodging for travellers
an ovation is enthusiastic applause or acclaim

explanation.surface: A hotel receives applause for doing things differently.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovation is a new method or idea, something altered from the usual.

clue.text: Fur's needed for the cold in the Orient

indicators.note: the word for cold goes inside the word for the Orient

parts.note: China is a country of the Orient, the East
a chill is coldness

explanation.surface: A fur coat is necessary for winter in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal; 'Fur's needed for' reads as a statement about winter clothing, but only 'Fur' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla is the soft grey pelt of a small South American rodent.

clue.text: Taking blockheads in is criminal!

parts.note: blockheads, plural, are two asses, fools
in is taken as written

explanation.surface: Being fooled by idiots is outrageous!
explanation.walkthrough: Two blockheads give ASS twice; 'Taking' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, a killer of a prominent person.

clue.text: Interfering with drainage could be a bloomer

indicators.note: interfering with the letters of the word means disturbing their order

explanation.surface: Tampering with the drains might be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interfering with' rearranges DRAINAGE. 'A bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardenia is a shrub grown for its fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Trick the top man in similar fashion

indicators.note: the word for the top man goes inside the word for similar

parts.note: in the same fashion means similarly
a king is the man at the top

explanation.surface: Fooling the boss in the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal. A skin game is an American term for a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin game is a dishonest scheme, a swindle or con.

clue.text: Polar explorer demanding hamper to go to the North

parts.note: to shackle is to hamper or restrain
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An Arctic traveller needing a basket before heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' suggests a picnic basket but is a verb, to restrain. Ernest Shackleton led Antarctic expeditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Shackleton was an Anglo-Irish leader of Antarctic expeditions.

clue.text: Notes resulting from a month on the road

parts.note: Oct is short for October
Ave is short for avenue, a road

explanation.surface: Messages arriving after spending a month travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like letters, but it is musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave is a span of eight musical notes.

clue.text: Go through a number with permission

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
leave means permission, as in leave to speak

explanation.surface: Passing through a crowd with consent.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split or cut through something.

clue.text: In general the eucalyptus tree thrives in the West Country

indicators.note: the answer sits within the general run of the words, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A gum tree flourishes generally in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: Street is a town in Somerset; the West Country is south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Street is a town in Somerset, a county of south-west England.

clue.text: Supplying assistance is excellent-sound

parts.note: A1 means first-class or excellent; the 1 is written as an I
a ding is a ringing sound

explanation.surface: Giving help is a great noise.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is first-rate, with the 1 written as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aiding means helping or giving support.

clue.text: The knight who's left an establishment crowd

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England, the established church
a lot is a group or crowd

explanation.surface: A knight who abandoned an institution full of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Establishment' is the Church of England, the established church, CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is a knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Error committed by poor sailor

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing or error
bad means poor in quality

explanation.surface: A mistake made by a hopeless seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad is the seafarer of the Arabian Nights tales.

clue.text: Address given for many years by the parson

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the period is put next to the clergyman

parts.note: a vicar is a parish priest, a parson
an age is a long period of years

explanation.surface: A sermon delivered over a long time by the clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a speech, but it is where someone lives, here a parson's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house of a vicar, a residence and so an address.

clue.text: Possibly ten are more elegant

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Perhaps ten people are better dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges TEN ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Neater means tidier or more stylish.

clue.text: Intrigue can bring profit

definitions.meaning: to intrigue someone is to arouse their curiosity
money earned on an investment or loan

explanation.definitionFit: To intrigue is to hold someone's attention; return paid on savings is a gain.
